blocks.x: How did all this affect Lester Young?

I don't think Lester ever recovered, really. You know, because the scene had changed so, and the army had probably demoralized Lester. I never could understand how they could keep a man of Lester's temperament in the army. You know, it probably -- I'm sure emotionally and otherwise it really took its toll on Lester.
Blesh says in his book, and I know you don't necessarily agree with Rush, but that Lester was I believe court-martialed while he was in the army.

And spent part of his time in prison. Supposedly over his possession of a pain killing pill which had been given him legitimately by an army base doctor after some kind of medical treatment. But that it was a case of racism, really.
And he was put away, locked up and according to Rush was never the same emotionally or physically (inaudible).
Well, I don't know what to attribute it to, because --
Was that your impression after he came out, that he was totally different, (inaudible).

Yeah, yeah. Well, something had happened to him when he came out. He seemed to have lost his fire, it seemed as if he was just burned out. You know, it wasn't the same Lester that I had known. And I attributed that to being in the army, and knowing Lester I just could never understand how they could keep him in the army because he wasn't psychologically or emotionally suited for this type of life. You know?
